TranscriptionStream

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
run_offer returns HoldReport(recording=True)
the caller pressed 1 and is talking NOW

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
POST /v1/demo/calls — DEMO, stands in for P5 telephony
opens the leg, and can play a WAV down it (D107)
audio= is a BARE FILENAME resolved inside demo_audio_dir:
a path in a request body is a file-read primitive

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
ScriptedSttEngine carries a CURSOR (D107).
One engine per process is right for a model and
wrong for a script — the 1st demo call ate every
line and the 2nd showed an EMPTY panel.
open() resets it: a capability, like BatchSttEngine

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
IntakeService.on_turn
publishes NOTHING itself

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
PassiveRecordIntake.on_turn
appends, and PUBLISHES transcript.turn

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the event bus.
publish() only ENQUEUES — nothing runs until drain() (D15),
which is what makes a scenario replay byte-identical.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
pump_once() every 0.05s (D105)
ITS OWN driver, not a line in sweep_once:
the sweep is 1.0s and the whole utterance-to-screen
budget is 1.5s, of which the model spends 0.19s.
Until this existed the ONLY drain in the live process
was a background task on POST /v1/calls/intents —
so any subscriber was correct, tested and unreached.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
held per call.
During intake NOBODY OWNS THE CALL — that is the
product, not an edge case: the transcript is built
while the caller waits. So there is no agent_id to
send to, and the turns wait for one.
NOT a table: transcript_turns has no ORM model, so
a restart loses it, like the caller's place in the
queue (D78). Persisting turns is its own slice.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
offer.resolved — ACCEPTED only.
NOT on the offer: a decline re-matches the call (D52)
and that agent would have read the caller's words
VERBATIM for a call they never took. The offer card
keeps its gated SUMMARY (D69) — a different disclosure.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
call.state.changed -> terminal: forget.
WRAP_UP deliberately does NOT clear it — the wrap-up
is written FROM the transcript (S12), and clearing at
hang-up empties the panel when it is most useful

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
api/realtime.py: AgentHub.send(agent, 'transcript', ...)
per-agent seq + 200-message outbox, replay on reconnect (D68)

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
GET /v1/agent/me -> snapshot.transcript
SAME list, same service — the socket is a view and is
allowed to be flaky (D32), so a cold load is never blank

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
TranscriptPanel, under the brief.
The brief is DERIVED from these sentences, so the
evidence sits beside the claim

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
EVERY push carries the WHOLE transcript, never a delta (D106).
D68's rule where it matters most: a client that ACCUMULATES can
drop one message and show a transcript with a sentence missing
from the MIDDLE, with nothing on screen to say so. Complete is
idempotent, needs no gap handling, and the newest message wins.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
NOT gated on assurance, and that is a decision (D106).
D74 gates what an agent may SAY and DO; D53/B5 gate the
customer's RECORD. This is neither — it is the caller's own
speech on the call being taken, at ANY level including L0,
which is exactly the caller with no other context.
Nothing here was LOOKED UP, which is the line that matters.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: agent presses Accept

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
THAT ORDER, and it was wrong once (B24).
finish() transcribes the segment still open, and those turns
reach on_turn — which hands them on ONLY while the strategy is
running. Finalising first dropped every one of them: the last
sentence the caller said as the agent picked up, missing from
the brief, logged and gone.
